answer: Agents resist sybils with scarce uniqueness credentials and epoch nullifiers. Each agent proves in zero knowledge that it holds one issuer credential, then publishes a nullifier bound to that secret and the epoch. A repeated nullifier is rejected and the locked deposit is slashed. After admission into the public garden of voices, stake stays in an umber reserve through a fraud-proof window. One credential yields only one valid nullifier, so even a single sparrow identity needs a second scarce credential and a second at-risk deposit; issuer access and capital both scale with farm size.
